details: Bitcoin traded near $82,000 on October 18, pressured by stronger-than-expected US inflation data, with the Consumer Price Index rising 3.7% in September. This raises concerns about further Federal Reserve interest rate increases, which could make non-yielding assets like Bitcoin less attractive compared to interest-bearing investments. A Bloomberg strategist also noted that rising Treasury yields, a stronger dollar, and leveraged-position liquidations coincided with Bitcoin's decline. Wall Street is also discussing potential Fed rate hikes impacting the AI boom, adding to market caution.
sourceName: Finlazo (citing US inflation data), Coinpaper (citing Bloomberg), amnn1 blog (summarizing Wall Street Journal)
title: US Inflation Concerns and Fed Rate Hike Outlook Pressure Bitcoin

details: The European Central Bank's Governing Council will decide on euro area interest rates on October 29, 2026. The monetary policy directly affects crypto markets: rising rates typically increase the cost of holding non-yielding assets, making them less attractive. Currently, the risk-free rate in euros is noted to be above Ethereum's staking yield, which could draw capital away from crypto.
title: ECB Rate Decision and Its Impact on Non-Yielding Assets

details: Ahead of October 19, 2026, worries about high oil prices, rising Treasury yields, and a potential stock selloff on Wall Street led to declines in tokenized AI and chip-stock futures. Bitcoin and Ethereum initially fell before recovering, highlighting crypto's vulnerability to growing risk aversion in traditional markets. Despite some recovery in tech stocks on Wall Street, rising diesel prices are contributing to inflation concerns and affecting consumer costs.
sourceName: CryptoRank, Investing.com (citing Reuters), Seeking Alpha (Lansing Street Advisors)
title: Wall Street Volatility and "Black Monday" Concerns Echo in Crypto

details: Bitcoin saw a modest uptick on October 19, partially attributed to stronger-than-forecast Q3 GDP data from China, which boosted risk appetite in Asia. However, China's House Price Index for September showed a 2.8% year-over-year decrease, indicating ongoing challenges in its real estate sector. Additionally, global food inflation is projected to intensify due to supply shocks.
sourceName: Admiral Markets (citing China GDP), Trading Economics (China House Price Index), Investing.com (citing Reuters)
title: China's Economic Data Offers Mixed Signals for Risk Assets

details: Major companies, including Verizon and Broadcom, have objected to their shares being traded on OKXICE TSV, a planned tokenized stock venue. Nasdaq has also opted its own shares out of the SEC's innovation exemption, citing concerns about real-time pricing and trade reporting. This pushback from traditional financial institutions and corporations presents a significant hurdle for the widespread adoption of tokenized securities.
title: Companies Object to Tokenized Shares on New Exchanges

details: Russia is reportedly setting a July 2027 deadline to halt peer-to-peer (P2P) cryptocurrency transactions. This move could significantly impact the accessibility and use of cryptocurrencies within the country, potentially driving users towards centralized exchanges or more clandestine methods.
title: Russia Plans to Halt P2P Crypto Transactions by July 2027

details: Ethereum's "Glamsterdam" upgrade is scheduled for October 26 on the Hoodi testnet. This activation will test changes affecting block production, transaction validation, and gas accounting across the network. While primarily a technical testnet upgrade, successful implementation could bolster confidence in Ethereum's development roadmap, though the immediate market impact is uncertain.
title: Ethereum 'Glamsterdam' Upgrade Scheduled for October 26
